title: Alaska’s ranked choice voting: Six years of experimenting and its biggest test yet
gist: Alaska is in its sixth year and third election under the ranked-choice-voting system created by a 2020 ballot measure, and in 2026 the system itself is on the ballot alongside Lisa Murkowski, the candidate it has both carried and sunk.

insights.claim: Alaska's ranked-choice-voting system, created by a 2020 ballot measure that also carried dark-money disclosure rules, is now in its sixth year and third election cycle.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Six years of returns make Alaska the longest-running U.S. test case for whether RCV changes candidate selection — the empirical base for RCV campaigns elsewhere.
insights.locator: Alaska is in its sixth year

insights.claim: The RCV system that remade Alaska's politics is itself back on the ballot, putting the rules and the politicians elected under them up for judgment simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: A repeal would be the first rollback of a statewide RCV regime and would reset expectations for electoral-reform measures in other states.
insights.quote: is back on the ballot, and so is a candidate it has both carried and sunk
insights.locator: The system that remade the state’s politics

insights.claim: Senator Lisa Murkowski is the emblematic case of the system's effects, having been both carried and sunk by ranked-choice voting.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Murkowski's fate is the clearest read on whether RCV structurally protects centrist incumbents against party bases.
insights.locator: Senator Lisa Murkowski departs from a lunch
